status.label: Verify existing recovery fixes
status.detail: Accidental Space activation and a stuck overlay are distinct. Merged fixes cover stale timers and focus-loss recovery, not a proven complete resolution of this report.

next_action.label: Compare activation and dismissal
next_action.reason: Check current behavior against the existing fixes before proposing another keyboard-state change.

judgment.rationale: The discussion supplies discriminating rapid-release and Space-activation cases. Related public fixes now exist, so first verify their coverage rather than invent duplicate implementation work.
evidence: https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/32047#issuecomment-2265828805 distinguishes accidental Space activation from remaining stuck.
https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/31988 documents similar stuck-toolbar cases and explicitly distinguishes same-window timing from focus-loss recovery.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce fast typing and rapid-release cases on a build containing both merged fixes; test focus change separately and only plan work for a remaining failure.

fix_assessment.rationale: PR 48944 invalidates stale delayed-render generations, and PR 50212 adds foreground-change recovery for an orphaned toolbar. They cover concrete portions of the reported family of failures. Neither proves that same-window rapid-release sticking or unwanted valid Space activation is resolved.

issue_context.summary: Quick Accent appears unexpectedly during typing and sometimes remains visible despite Escape or clicking away. The discussion separates accidental activation from failure to dismiss.
known_information: Original version is 0.77.0 from Microsoft Store; a commenter associates sticking with releasing the shortcut too quickly.
Space is an activation key in the discussed configuration, making a held final letter plus Space a possible normal trigger.
The related issue 31988 remains open and contains both focus-loss and same-window timing reports.
PR 48944 merged on 2026-07-01; PR 50212 merged on 2026-09-11. The latter explicitly leaves same-window lost-key-up recovery outside its scope.
The live issue has no assignees; no outstanding reporter request is present.
inferences: Some apparently random invocations may be valid activations rather than a defect.
A residual same-window timing failure may remain even when foreground-change recovery works.
issue_context.analysis: The current maintainable next step is a local coverage matrix for the existing fixes, not a blanket duplicate closure or a new timer/watchdog plan. No current-build behavioral test was performed in this pass.
initial_investigation: Read all four original comments and all linked 31988 discussion, plus the complete public cross-reference timeline.
Read the descriptions and merged states of PRs 48944, 49701 and 50212; press-and-hold isolation in 49701 is separate from legacy Space activation.
Current KeyboardListener.cpp registers a foreground event hook; PowerAccent.cs uses DelayedDisplayState, consistent with the existing recovery and render-generation work.
Similarity-only references do not establish that the entire original issue is a duplicate.

information_gaps.information: Which failure modes remain on a build containing the merged recovery changes.
information_gaps.why_needed: Avoids reimplementing a merged fix and separates unwanted activation policy from stale visible state.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Maintainer: run the activation/dismissal matrix below with Space enabled and disabled, both with and without a foreground-window change.

reproduce.title: Separate accidental Quick Accent activation from a stuck toolbar
reproduce.version_requirement: A current build containing merged PRs 48944 and 50212; original report used 0.77.0.
prerequisites: Use Notepad and a second ordinary application, with one accent-capable language set enabled.
Record activation mode and input delay; use a legacy Space/arrow mode, not press-and-hold, for the original case.
steps: Enable Space activation and type ordinary words rapidly, overlapping the final letter with Space; distinguish a legitimate invocation from an orphaned toolbar.
Deliberately invoke an accent and release the letter and trigger rapidly near the configured delay, repeating without changing foreground window.
Repeat, but switch foreground application with the mouse while the toolbar is visible; confirm it dismisses without inserting an unwanted character.
Use arrows-only activation and repeat ordinary typing to separate the Space-trigger configuration from dismissal failures.
For any residual failure, record the precise mode, delay, release order and whether a foreground change occurred before changing code.
reproduce.expected_result: A finished or cancelled gesture must not leave a stale toolbar. Focus-loss recovery and stale-timer cancellation should work; valid Space activation alone is not evidence of a bug.
